record.context_brief: Topological invariance of Hodge and Chern data
record.original_question: Which rational linear combinations of Hodge numbers and Chern characteristic numbers of a smooth complex projective variety are topological invariants, under oriented or unoriented homeomorphism or diffeomorphism, and which are not?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Are the h^{p,q} and the Chern characteristic numbers of an algebraic variety Vn topological invariants of Vn? If not, determine all those linear combinations of the h^{p,q} and the Chern characteristic numbers which are topological invariants.

Progress and solutions. I believe the only problem from [Hi54] that was wide open in 1987 and has since been solved completely, is Problem 31, about the topological (non-)invariance of characteristic numbers of algebraic varieties, whose solution is described at the end of this report.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a smooth complex projective variety of complex dimension $n$. For $0\le p,q\le n$ let $h^{p,q}(V)=\dim_{\mathbb{C}} H^q(V,\Omega^p_V)$ denote its Hodge numbers, and let the Chern characteristic numbers of $V$ be the integers obtained by evaluating monomials of total weight $n$ in the Chern classes $c_1(TV),\dots,c_n(TV)\in H^*(V,\mathbb{Z})$ on the fundamental class $[V]$.

Consider rational linear combinations
$$L = \sum_{p,q} a_{p,q}\, h^{p,q} + \sum_{|I|=n} b_I\, c_I,$$
where $a_{p,q},b_I\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $c_I$ ranges over Chern monomials of degree $n$.

Determine, in each of the four equivalence relations on smooth complex projective varieties given by
(a) orientation-preserving diffeomorphism, (b) unoriented diffeomorphism, (c) orientation-preserving homeomorphism, (d) unoriented homeomorphism,
exactly which such linear combinations $L$ are invariant. In particular, decide whether the individual Hodge numbers $h^{p,q}$ and the individual Chern numbers $c_I$ are themselves invariants under each of these relations, and if not, characterize the full $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space of those that are.
artifact.category_tag: Hodge and Chern numbers of projective varieties
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved. Kotschick proved that a rational linear combination of Chern numbers of smooth complex projective varieties is an oriented diffeomorphism invariant iff it is a linear combination of the Euler number and the Pontryagin numbers, and is a homeomorphism invariant iff it is a multiple of the Euler number. Kotschick and Schreieder then determined the Hodge ring of Kähler manifolds and combined it with the unitary bordism ring to characterize all rational linear combinations of Hodge numbers and Chern numbers that are (oriented/unoriented) homeomorphism or diffeomorphism invariants, completing the solution.

status_evidence.title: The Hodge ring of Kaehler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Combining the Hodge ring with the unitary bordism ring, we treat linear combinations of Hodge and Chern numbers, leading to a complete solution of a classical problem of Hirzebruch.
status_evidence.claim: Kotschick–Schreieder give a complete solution of Hirzebruch's problem on linear combinations of Hodge and Chern numbers.

status_evidence.title: Characteristic numbers of algebraic varieties (Kotschick, PNAS)
status_evidence.snippet: A rational linear combination of Chern numbers is an oriented diffeomorphism invariant of smooth complex projective varieties iff it is a linear combination of the Euler and Pontryagin numbers; a homeomorphism invariant iff it is a multiple of the Euler number.
status_evidence.claim: Kotschick fully resolved the Chern-number part of the question.
